hook: An FBI FD-302 interview record documents a first-hand account by a witness with fifteen years of experience at a U.S. test site who observed a silent cigar-shaped object with an intense diamond-white light hovering above a restricted test range on the morning of September 2023, before it vanished instantaneously in a clear sky.
why_it_matters: The witness's professional context — fifteen years at a military test facility with direct familiarity with U.S. aircraft and drones — lends the account unusual credibility, and the sighting occurred within restricted military airspace the witness herself had arranged to close for that day's tests. The object's instantaneous disappearance without contrails in clear sky, its silence, and its apparent size (two to three Blackhawk helicopters in length) rule out conventional explanations the witness would have been well-positioned to recognize. The anomalous gate malfunction immediately preceding the sighting adds an unexplained environmental correlate.

key_findings.finding: The witness observed a cigar-shaped object described as 'metallic bronze in color' — notably different from the 'metallic/gray' descriptor in the war.gov manifest — with an intense diamond-white light on its eastern end, hovering 500 to 3,000 feet above the tree line approximately one mile from her position.

quotes.text: cigar shaped object with an extremely bright light southwest of them approximately 500 to 3000 feet above the nearest tree line (agent note: the tree line was approximately one mile south west of JJ position).
The object was "metallic bronze in color" and was the length of two or three Blackhawk helicopters lined up nose to tail.

key_findings.finding: The object vanished instantaneously in a clear, cloudless sky after five to ten seconds of observation, leaving no contrails, and was not seen again despite an active search of the sky.

quotes.text: They watched the object for five to ten seconds and then the object just disappeared. The sky was clear with no clouds and the object did leave any contrails.
searched the sky but did not see the object again.

key_findings.finding: An anomalous gate malfunction — the gate opening partially and closing on three successive remote attempts before finally opening on the fourth — occurred immediately before the sighting, and the gate had no prior or subsequent operational issues.

quotes.text: attempted to open the gate remotely using a fob. The gate opened just a little and then closed on three separate tries. On the fourth attempt the gate opened completely and stayed open. There were no prior operational problems with that particular gate and there were no operating issues with the gate after September

key_findings.finding: The witness had restricted the airspace for that morning's tests, immediately recognized the object was not an aircraft or drone, and reported no engine interference from her vehicle while the object was visible.

quotes.text: was initially annoyed when she saw the object because she had restricted the ranges for the tests they were going to conduct that morning but then she realized the object was not an aircraft or drone.
did not notice any interference with her vehicle's engine while the object was visible.

key_findings.finding: The witness's credibility is bolstered by fifteen years of experience at the facility and familiarity with most U.S. military aircraft and drones; a second witness in the convoy independently confirmed the sighting; and the primary witness stated she would not have reported the object had she seen it alone.

did not have reported the object if she had seen it by herself. Several of her co-workers subsequently made fun of her due to her report.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: This is a contemporary (2023) UAP report from personnel at a U.S. military test facility, precisely the category of case AARO was established to collect and assess.

The sighting occurred at a U.S. test site with restricted airspace, contractor personnel working on a 'special project,' and a witness with fifteen years of classified test-site experience — characteristics consistent with the classified test range environment, though the specific site is redacted.
Wright-Patterson has historically been the repository for military UAP physical evidence and reports; a documented sighting at an active U.S. test site would plausibly feed into that reporting chain.
